annotations.text:
THE INTAKE — paid, six screens.
The order is the product: what is fixed, who is affected, what you have, the money, what you would trade, and only then where you want to end up.

THE MAP — the same product, both directions. JAKE closes the gap by earning more. MARCUS closes it by needing less, and his plan crosses OUT starting a business. One example is one product; this is why there are two.
THE FREE DIAGNOSTIC — public, six taps, rules not a model. Naming what does NOT fit is what earns the next click.

HERO = THE PRODUCT. From the omen.trade reference — what is worth taking is not the darkness, it is that the PRODUCT is the hero, floating with depth, ambient light moving BEHIND while the type stays still, one colour doing the work.

My earlier mockups had no product on them at all, which is why two directions read as no change.

Same composition, two grounds — the question is whether this survives going dark, or whether dark + green reads as the trading-platform neighbourhood this audience has been burned by.

ATMOSPHERE — why anyone stops.

Both lead with the DESTINATION, which no screen in the product has ever shown: it is all process, and we ask someone to describe their Tuesday and never reflect it back. "An ordinary Tuesday" is deliberately the anti-lambo.

A / WARM AND MADE — buildable today, no photography. The dotted path with three marks is the product's own metaphor and the same spine the map draws.
B / PHOTOGRAPHIC — higher ceiling, needs a real photograph. THE IMAGE HERE IS DRAWN: judge the composition, not the picture.

THE OPENING SCREEN — three bets on the first fifteen seconds, same visual system.

RECOGNITION names something true about the reader — safest, but still asks to be believed.
DEMONSTRATION shows the shape of an answer before asking for anything — strongest proof, shows the hand early.
QUESTION starts being useful immediately — best completion, but a stranger has been told nothing, and it can read as a quiz funnel.
